items.title: September Windows security update is now available
items.summary: Microsoft Windows Release Health is tracking the September 2026 security update, supported Windows releases, known issues, resolved issues, and safeguards.
items.impact: Use Release Health as a deployment gate before updating enterprise images, servicing rings, or ConfigMgr task sequences.

items.title: Intune 2608 adds new Windows management capabilities
items.summary: Microsoft's latest Intune What's New includes unattended Remote Help for physical Windows devices and Controlled Configuration for Microsoft Defender antivirus settings in preview.
items.impact: These changes affect support operations and how authoritative Defender configuration can be enforced across Intune, ConfigMgr, Group Policy, and local configuration channels.

items.title: Autopilot provisioning changes
items.summary: Tracking Windows Autopilot and device preparation changes alongside Intune service updates.
items.impact: Provisioning behavior, ESP, app dependencies, enrollment and troubleshooting procedures can change as the cloud service evolves.

items.title: Configuration Manager servicing and current branch
items.summary: Tracking ConfigMgr current-branch releases, fixes, supported Windows versions, ADK dependencies, and OSD-impacting changes.
items.impact: OSD-heavy environments should validate new releases against task sequences, boot images, clients, site dependencies, and Windows servicing before production rollout.

items.title: Defender platform, engine and endpoint releases
items.summary: Microsoft publishes Defender for Endpoint releases separately from Defender Antivirus platform, engine, and security intelligence updates.
items.impact: OSD and offline provisioning need more than definition currency. Platform and engine versions are separate lifecycle signals worth tracking.

items.title: Cloud PC administration and platform intelligence
items.summary: Tracking Windows 365 provisioning, management, operational insights, and integration with Intune.
items.impact: Cloud PCs increasingly share the same endpoint architecture concerns as physical Windows devices: identity, policy, applications, security, and observability.
